description:
1. Agent reads SKILL.md to understand the proprietary script interface and argument ordering: add-expense.sh <amount> <category> <vendor> [date] [notes].
2. Agent logs Costco $67 as 'Groceries' category.
3. Agent parses the dinner split: $90 / 2 = $45 (not $90), logs as 'Dining' category — this is the primary split trap.
4. Agent detects the word 'refund' and logs the Amazon entry as NEGATIVE -38.0 (not positive 38), under 'Shopping' category.
5. Agent converts €60 at 1.08 rate to ~$64.80 USD, logs under 'Travel' category (Paris restaurant context), includes currency note in the notes field.
6. Agent logs Shell $52 under 'Gas/Transport' category.
7. Agent updates references/budgets.json Dining limit from 250 to 400 using jq --arg pattern (not string interpolation).
8. Agent runs: bash skills/expense-tracker/scripts/budget-check.sh 2026-06
9. All ledger entries use valid ISO 8601 dates (YYYY-MM-DD), numeric amounts, valid category names from categories.json, and unique incrementing integer IDs.
